light_description: Core Virtues fuzz, introduced as the builder's second model in 2019; a Fuzz Face-family design developed from the builder's vintage Dallas Arbiter reference. Surviving dealer and CULT pages provide exterior product photography and lineage information.

Core Virtues distortion introduced after the 2019 Monica/Lander pair; official/dealer material describes low-gain crunch through higher-gain drive and documents bipolar-transistor plus LED combination clipping. Dealer documentation preserves the early RAT/Fringe Logo inspiration.

Core Virtues overdrive released after Stella; current dealer documentation describes its deliberately translucent rather than fully transparent voicing and a gain range extending from clean through classical distortion.

CULT-limited Stella-descendant based on an earlier Stella prototype; retained as a separate edition relationship because it has its own retail identity, while its lineage remains subordinate to Stella.
Artist/signature presentation of the Monica platform; retained as a relationship-only signature variant rather than a new core conceptual model.
CULT-limited presentation of arca with its own retail identity and exterior photography; retained as a relationship edition pending stronger evidence of a distinct core circuit family.
Historical CULT limited Lander based on a 1966-68 germanium-transistor Fuzz Face reference; retained as a relationship edition of Lander rather than a separate central family.
Historical CULT limited Lander based on a 1969-73 silicon-transistor Fuzz Face reference; retained as a relationship edition of Lander rather than a separate central family.
Later CULT limited Lander that combines and refines the iss.1 germanium and iss.2 silicon reference concepts into one product; retained as a relationship edition of Lander.
Virtues-associated full-tube booster; retained as a scope-boundary relationship record because its primary category is booster rather than central overdrive/distortion/fuzz.
